name: toggle-button
title: Toggle button
purpose: A button that turns one view option on or off, such as Wrap lines, and says which with aria-pressed.
whenToUse: For an option of the current view that takes effect at once and is not saved as a setting: Wrap lines, Show whitespace, Show tool calls.
In a toolbar above a log, a diff or a transcript, in its small size.
whenNotToUse: For a setting that is stored, in a settings form. Use a switch, or a checkbox when it is sent with the form.
To choose one of several views, such as Unified or Split. Use a segmented control.
For an option with only an icon. Use an icon button with aria-pressed.
For an action that happens once, such as Copy. Use a button.

variants.name: off
variants.use: aria-pressed="false". Drawn as a plain button.

variants.name: on
variants.use: aria-pressed="true". A stronger border, a sunken fill and a bar under the label.

sizes.name: default
sizes.use: As tall as a control: 40px by default and 44px on a coarse pointer.

sizes.name: small
sizes.use: The button component's small size: drawn 32px tall for a toolbar, with a 44px pointer target on a coarse pointer. Lay small toggles out with ds-cluster ds-gap-lg, so the targets of two wrapped rows do not overlap.

accessibility: Use a button element with type="button", the classes ds-button and ds-toggle-button, and aria-pressed set to "true" or "false". The attribute is always present, so a screen reader announces a toggle button in both states.
The label names the option and stays the same in both states: Wrap lines, never Unwrap lines. Only aria-pressed changes. An icon is decoration and carries aria-hidden="true".
The app flips aria-pressed on each press and applies the option at once. Nothing else is needed: the styles read aria-pressed only.
Never add ds-button--primary to show that an option is on.
Group related toggles in an element with role="group" and an aria-label that says what they change, such as Diff view options.
Tab reaches each toggle, and Enter and Space flip it. Both come from the button element.
Set the disabled attribute while the option cannot change. The bar stays, so the reader can still see which options were on.
A toggle button is never busy: the bar is drawn where the button component draws its spinner.
